question: Which great leader died due to his injuries in the Anti-Simon Commission Protest of 1928?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lala Lajpat Rai.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai** was a prominent **Indian freedom fighter** and leader of the** Indian National Congress.**
 
• He was a vocal opponent of **British rule in India** and played a key role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• In **1928**, he led a protest against the **Simon Commission**, a British government initiative to review the Indian constitution, which was seen as an attempt to prolong **British rule.**
 
• During the protest, Lala Lajpat Rai was brutally beaten by the** police** and sustained **serious injuries.**
 
• He **died **a few weeks later.
 
• His death sparked widespread outrage and further fuelled the** Indian independence movement.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lala Hardayal **was another Indian freedom fighter and founder of the** Ghadar Party,** which was dedicated to the overthrow of British rule in India.

 
 
• He died **March 4, 1939.**
 
 
 
• **Bhagat Singh** was a **revolutionary socialist** who played a key role in the Indian independence movement.
 
 
• He was **executed** by the British government in **1931.**
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** was a prominent **Indian nationalist and social reformer** who advocated for **Indian self-rule **and played a key role in the Indian National Congress.
 
 
• He died in **1920.**
